definitions.meaning: What the air is doing on one day: sun, wind, clouds and rain today.
The pattern of weather over many years, not one cold or hot day.
The source of heat in the chain: the sun heats the land.
Air warmed by the heated land: it rises above the land.
Cooler air that flows in to take the place of the risen warm air.
Cooled air gathered high up into visible drops of water.
Drops in the clouds grown heavy, falling back to the ground.

mechanismSteps: The sun heats the land: the sun pours heat onto the land, and the land warms the air above it so the warm air begins to rise.
Warm air rises, cool air flows in: the warm air climbs, cooler air flows in to take its place, and that moving air is wind.
Clouds gather, rain falls: high up the warm air cools and gathers into clouds, and the drops grow heavy and fall as rain.
objectives: Explain how the sun heats the land and sets the air moving
Describe how warm air rises, cool air flows in, and clouds bring rain
Tell weather apart from climate and give the meaning of each
subject: geography
title: Weather and climate: heat on the move

trap.explanation: One day of weather feels like the whole climate, so a single day is read as the trend. Today's weather is not the climate: climate is the pattern of weather over many years, not one cold or hot day. In class, compare one cold morning (weather) with records over many years (climate): only the long pattern can show whether the climate itself is changing.
trap.misconception: A cold day today means the climate is getting colder.

workedExample: Follow the heat as a worked example: first the sun heats the land and the land warms the air above it. Next the warm air rises, cool air flows in to take its place, and that moving air is wind. High up the risen air cools, clouds gather, rain falls back to the ground. So the whole chain is: sun heats the land -> warm air rises and cool air flows in -> clouds gather and rain falls.
